findings.title: Left-handed Matrix factories
findings.snippet: var view = Matrix.LookAtLH(new Vector3(0f, 0f, -5f), Vector3.Zero, Vector3.UnitY);

triggeredRules.title: SharpDX assembly reference
triggeredRules.explanation: The project references SharpDX assemblies (SharpDX, SharpDX.Toolkit.*, SharpDX.Direct3D11 and others). They come from the SharpDX 2.x NuGet packages, which target .NET Framework 4.x and need the SharpDX build targets. They are not part of MonoGame.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator writes an SDK-style project that drops every SharpDX reference and references MonoGame instead. Code that used SharpDX types directly is reported by the SDX005 to SDX008 and SDX034 to SDX035 rules.

triggeredRules.title: SharpDX build targets import
triggeredRules.explanation: The project imports SharpDX.targets or SharpDX.Toolkit.targets from the NuGet packages folder. Those files set the reference paths and run the Toolkit content compilers. They exist only after a NuGet restore of the old packages, and a build without them stops with MSB4019.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator drops the imports, the NuGet restore guard target and the import stamp from the SDK-style project it writes.

triggeredRules.title: .NET Framework 4.x target
triggeredRules.explanation: The project targets .NET Framework 4.x (for example v4.5). MonoGame 3.8.6.1 desktop projects target net8.0.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator writes an SDK-style project for net8.0 (or the Windows variant for WindowsDX).

triggeredRules.title: Direct use of SharpDX.Direct3D11
triggeredRules.explanation: The code uses the raw Direct3D 11 API through SharpDX.Direct3D11. MonoGame has no such layer. Code written against devices, contexts and buffers has to be rewritten against the MonoGame graphics API. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Rewrite the affected code with MonoGame GraphicsDevice, VertexBuffer, IndexBuffer and Effect types. This cannot be automated.

triggeredRules.title: Direct use of SharpDX.DXGI
triggeredRules.explanation: The code uses SharpDX.DXGI, usually for pixel formats and swap chain settings. Formats map to MonoGame SurfaceFormat in simple cases, but not by name. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Replace each DXGI format or setting with the MonoGame equivalent (SurfaceFormat, PresentationParameters) by hand.

triggeredRules.title: Toolkit game namespace
triggeredRules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX.Toolkit, which holds Game, GameTime and GraphicsDeviceManager. The same names live in Microsoft.Xna.Framework in MonoGame. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.

triggeredRules.title: Toolkit graphics namespace
triggeredRules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX.Toolkit.Graphics (SpriteBatch, Texture2D, SpriteFont, BasicEffect). MonoGame keeps these names in Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.

triggeredRules.title: SharpDX math namespace
triggeredRules.explanation: The code imports SharpDX for its math types (Vector2, Vector3, Matrix, Color, Rectangle). MonoGame keeps these names in Microsoft.Xna.Framework. Types that exist only in SharpDX are reported by SDX034 and SDX035. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the using directive to Microsoft.Xna.Framework.

triggeredRules.title: Left-handed Matrix factories
triggeredRules.explanation: The code builds left-handed matrices. XNA and MonoGame are right-handed. A rename would be wrong, because winding order and view direction change with the handedness. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Convert the scene to right-handed coordinates (flip Z and the triangle winding), then use the Create* factories.

triggeredRules.title: Vector3.TransformCoordinate
triggeredRules.explanation: TransformCoordinate divides by w. MonoGame Vector3.Transform does not. The result is the same for affine matrices and different for projection matrices. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Use Vector3.Transform for affine matrices. For a projection, transform as Vector4 and divide by w.

triggeredRules.title: RectangleF
triggeredRules.explanation: RectangleF is a SharpDX type with float fields. MonoGame has no such type, and SpriteBatch.Draw takes a Rectangle with integer fields. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Use Rectangle, or add a small struct of your own. With the compatibility shims on, the migrated copy gets a RectangleF stand-in (sharpdx-toolkit task 14) and no marker.

triggeredRules.title: Color4 and Color3
triggeredRules.explanation: Color4 and Color3 are float color structs of SharpDX. MonoGame has Color (bytes) and Vector4 (floats) but no type of this name. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Use Color for byte colors or Vector4 for float colors. With the compatibility shims on, the migrated copy gets Color4 and Color3 stand-ins (sharpdx-toolkit task 14) and no marker.

triggeredRules.title: SetRenderTargets (depth buffer or several targets)
triggeredRules.explanation: The code passes a depth buffer or several targets to SetRenderTargets. In MonoGame a render target owns its depth buffer, and several targets are set with SetRenderTargets(RenderTargetBinding[]). Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Create each render target with the depth format it needs and set them with SetRenderTargets(params RenderTargetBinding[]).

triggeredRules.title: RenderTarget2D.New
triggeredRules.explanation: RenderTarget2D.New is a static factory that takes a DXGI PixelFormat and a mip map count. MonoGame uses a constructor with SurfaceFormat and DepthFormat. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Call new RenderTarget2D(device, width, height, mipMap, SurfaceFormat.Color, DepthFormat.Depth24) and pick the formats by hand.

triggeredRules.title: GeometricPrimitive
triggeredRules.explanation: GeometricPrimitive (cube, sphere, teapot and so on) has no MonoGame equivalent. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Build the vertex and index buffers yourself, or load a model for the shape.

triggeredRules.title: DrawQuad
triggeredRules.explanation: GraphicsDevice.DrawQuad draws a full-screen quad. MonoGame has no such call. Matching is by syntax only, so a look-alike name in unrelated code can match.
triggeredRules.resolution: Draw a full-screen SpriteBatch pass instead.
